network-security.title: TCP Three-Way Handshake
network-security.summary: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK establishes a stateful TCP connection. RST terminates abruptly; FIN closes gracefully.
network-security.detail: The handshake synchronizes initial sequence numbers and negotiates connection state in both directions. Half-open scans exploit stopping after SYN-ACK. Firewalls and IDS often key on SYN rate and incomplete handshakes.

network-security.title: ARP Spoofing — Layer 2 MITM
network-security.summary: Forged ARP replies poison a victim's cache so traffic routes through the attacker on the local segment.
network-security.detail: ARP has no authentication — any host can claim to own an IP. Attackers flood gratuitous ARP to maintain poisoned entries. Defense: dynamic ARP inspection on switches, static ARP for gateways, encryption above L2.

network-security.title: DNS Zone Transfer (AXFR)
network-security.summary: AXFR dumps an entire DNS zone if misconfigured — exposes internal hostnames and network topology.
network-security.detail: Legitimate between primary/secondary DNS. Attackers query `dig axfr` against authoritative servers. Restrict with `allow-transfer` ACLs in BIND.

network-security.title: Wireshark — Display Filters
network-security.summary: Display filters trim the packet list post-capture; syntax differs from capture filters (BPF/tcpdump).
network-security.detail: Use `ip.addr`, `tcp.port`, `http.request`, `tls.handshake.type`. Combine with `&&` and `||`. Follow TCP stream to reconstruct sessions.

network-security.title: VLAN Hopping
network-security.summary: Double-tagging or switch spoofing tricks a switch into forwarding frames to another VLAN.
network-security.detail: Mitigate with explicit trunk port config, disable DTP, native VLAN mismatch checks, and place management VLAN separately.

network-security.title: iptables — Stateful Filtering
network-security.summary: `-m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED` allows return traffic without opening inbound ports broadly.
network-security.detail: Stateful firewalls track connection state in conntrack. Default-drop INPUT with explicit allow for needed services. Log dropped packets sparingly to avoid DoS via log flooding.

commands.cmd: sudo iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
commands.explain: Allow return traffic for outbound connections

web-security.title: SQL Injection — UNION-Based
web-security.summary: UNION SELECT appends attacker-controlled rows when input is concatenated into SQL without parameterization.
web-security.detail: Find column count with `ORDER BY n` or `UNION SELECT null,...`. Extract schema from information_schema. Fix with prepared statements and ORM parameter binding.

web-security.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
web-security.summary: Reflected XSS executes in victim browser from crafted URL; stored XSS persists in server-side data (comments, profiles).
web-security.detail: Defense: context-aware output encoding, CSP, HttpOnly cookies for session tokens. DOM XSS bypasses server if JS writes untrusted input to DOM.

web-security.title: CSRF — Token & SameSite Defenses
web-security.summary: CSRF tricks a logged-in browser into submitting unwanted state-changing requests. Sync tokens + SameSite cookies mitigate.
web-security.detail: Use unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens tied to session. SameSite=Lax/Strict reduces cross-origin cookie submission. Verify Origin/Referer on sensitive POSTs.

web-security.title: OWASP Top 10 — Priority Web Risks
web-security.summary: Broken access control and injection consistently rank highest — map findings to Top 10 for stakeholder communication.
web-security.detail: Use Top 10 as a coverage checklist in assessments, not an exhaustive list. Pair with ASVS for depth.

exploitation-vulnerability.title: Buffer Overflow — Stack Layout
exploitation-vulnerability.summary: Overflowing a stack buffer can overwrite saved return address — classic path to arbitrary code execution before mitigations.
exploitation-vulnerability.detail: Layout: buffer → saved EBP → return address. Modern mitigations: ASLR, stack canaries, NX/DEP. Bypass techniques include ROP and info leaks.

exploitation-vulnerability.title: ROP — Return-Oriented Programming
exploitation-vulnerability.summary: Chain existing code gadgets ending in `ret` to execute syscalls when NX blocks shellcode on stack.
exploitation-vulnerability.detail: Find gadgets in binary/libs. Build chain to call mprotect or execve. Defenses: CET, shadow stack, ASLR with high entropy.

exploitation-vulnerability.title: Spectre & Meltdown — CPU Side Channels
exploitation-vulnerability.summary: Speculative execution leaks data across isolation boundaries via cache timing — patch OS/microcode, isolate VMs.
exploitation-vulnerability.detail: Meltdown: user read kernel memory. Spectre: trick victim into speculatively loading secret. Mitigations impact performance (KPTI, retpoline).

reconnaissance-osint.title: Nmap — Stealth SYN Scan
reconnaissance-osint.summary: -sS sends SYN without completing handshake. Faster than connect scan, historically quieter. Requires root.
reconnaissance-osint.detail: Open: SYN-ACK then RST. Closed: RST. Filtered: no response. Combine with `-Pn` when ICMP blocked.

reconnaissance-osint.title: Shodan — Internet Asset Discovery
reconnaissance-osint.summary: Shodan indexes banners and service metadata — find exposed ICS, RDP, default creds interfaces.
reconnaissance-osint.detail: Query by org, product, vuln tags. Pair with legal scope. Complement active nmap on in-scope CIDR.

commands.explain: Find HTTPS services for an organization

reconnaissance-osint.title: Google Dorking — Search Operator OSINT
reconnaissance-osint.summary: Advanced search operators surface indexed files, login pages, and error messages: `site:`, `filetype:`, `inurl:`.
reconnaissance-osint.detail: Examples: `site:target.com filetype:pdf`, `inurl:admin login`. Cache and robots.txt reveal paths.

commands.explain: Hunt leaked config/SQL dumps indexed by Google

cryptography.title: TLS Handshake & Certificate Validation
cryptography.summary: Client verifies server cert chain to trusted CA, checks hostname (SAN), validity period, and revocation status.
cryptography.detail: Handshake negotiates cipher suite and establishes session keys. Pinning mitigates rogue CA risk. Monitor for weak protocols (TLS 1.0/1.1).

commands.explain: Inspect cert chain and negotiated cipher

cryptography.title: AES — GCM vs CBC Mode
cryptography.summary: GCM provides authenticated encryption (AEAD); CBC requires separate MAC and is vulnerable to padding oracle if misimplemented.
cryptography.detail: Prefer AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305. Never reuse nonce/IV with same key in GCM.

cryptography.title: Kerberos — TGT & TGS Flow
cryptography.summary: AS-REQ/REP issues TGT; TGS-REQ/REP grants service tickets. Golden ticket forges TGT with krbtgt hash.
cryptography.detail: Watch for Kerberoasting (offline crack service tickets), AS-REP roasting (no preauth), and pass-the-ticket.

linux-cli.title: find — SUID & Writable Path Discovery
linux-cli.summary: find locates SUID binaries and world-writable directories — common privesc enumeration step.
linux-cli.detail: SUID binaries with shell escape = root. Writable `/etc/passwd` or cron paths enable persistence.

linux-cli.title: grep — Recursive Content Search
linux-cli.summary: `-r` searches directories; `-i` case insensitive; `-l` files-only. Essential for CTF and log triage.
linux-cli.detail: Combine with `find ... -exec grep` for filtered paths. Use `--color` and `-n` line numbers.

linux-cli.title: SSH — Key-Based Authentication
linux-cli.summary: Public-key auth beats passwords; disable PasswordAuthentication after key deploy. Use `-i` for key path.
linux-cli.detail: Permissions: `~/.ssh` 700, authorized_keys 600. Fail2ban for brute force. Jump hosts for bastion access.

commands.explain: Connect with specific key and port

malware-threat.title: YARA — Pattern Matching for Malware
malware-threat.summary: YARA rules match strings/hex/regex with conditions — scan files, memory, or traffic at scale.
malware-threat.detail: Structure: meta, strings, condition. Use `pe` module for PE headers. Test false positive rate on clean corpus.

malware-threat.title: Static vs Dynamic Malware Analysis
malware-threat.summary: Static: strings, imports, disasm without execution. Dynamic: sandbox behavior, network IOCs, API calls.
malware-threat.detail: Combine both. Packers/obfuscation defeat static — dynamic in isolated VM. Watch anti-VM checks.

malware-threat.title: MITRE ATT&CK — Tactic Mapping
malware-threat.summary: Map observed behaviors to ATT&CK tactics/techniques for detection engineering and reporting consistency.
malware-threat.detail: Use technique IDs in Sigma rules and detection gaps analysis. Navigator layers visualize coverage.

digital-forensics.title: Chain of Custody
digital-forensics.summary: Document who handled evidence, when, and why — breaks in chain jeopardize admissibility.
digital-forensics.detail: Use write blockers for disks. Cryptographic hashes (SHA-256) on acquisition. Store master images read-only; work on copies.

digital-forensics.title: Memory Forensics — Volatility Basics
digital-forensics.summary: RAM captures reveal running processes, network connections, keys, and malware not yet on disk.
digital-forensics.detail: Profile must match kernel. Hunt injected code, hollowed processes, and command lines in `_EPROCESS`.

digital-forensics.title: Disk Imaging with dd
digital-forensics.summary: Bit-for-bit copy with `dd` or `dc3dd` (logging). Verify with hash before analysis.
digital-forensics.detail: Always use hardware write blocker. Record serial numbers and tool versions in case notes.

commands.cmd: sudo dd if=/dev/sdb of=evidence.img bs=4M status=progress

cloud-infrastructure.title: AWS IAM — Least Privilege
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Grant minimum actions/resources required. Avoid `*` in production policies; use roles not long-lived keys.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Enable MFA on root and admins. Use IAM Access Analyzer and policy simulator. Rotate access keys.

cloud-infrastructure.title: S3 — Public Bucket Misconfiguration
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Block Public Access at account level; audit ACLs and bucket policies for `Principal: *`.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Common breach vector. Use Macie and Config rules. Encrypt at rest with KMS.

cloud-infrastructure.title: CloudTrail — API Audit Logging
cloud-infrastructure.summary: CloudTrail records management events — enable organization trail, log file validation, S3 lifecycle protection.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Pair with CloudWatch alarms on root login, IAM changes, and security group opens.

cloud-infrastructure.title: AWS VPC — Security Groups vs NACLs
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Security groups are stateful instance-level firewalls; NACLs are stateless subnet-level filters evaluated in order.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Default deny outbound is rare in SGs but possible in NACLs. Least-privilege inbound rules per tier. Log rejected flows with VPC Flow Logs.

cloud-infrastructure.title: EC2 — Instance Hardening Baseline
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Disable unnecessary services, patch AMIs, use IMDSv2, restrict SSH to bastion, and attach instance profiles instead of static keys.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Use Systems Manager Session Manager for shell access without open port 22. Enable EBS encryption by default. Tag instances for ownership and environment.

cloud-infrastructure.title: AWS KMS — Key Management
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Customer-managed CMKs give rotation and policy control; envelope encryption wraps data keys for S3, EBS, and RDS.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Separate keys per environment. Monitor CloudTrail for DisableKey and ScheduleKeyDeletion. Use grants sparingly.

cloud-infrastructure.title: CloudWatch — Security Event Alarms
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Metric filters on CloudTrail log groups can alarm on root login, IAM policy changes, and failed console logins.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Route alarms to SNS → ticketing. Tune thresholds to avoid alert fatigue. Combine with GuardDuty findings for correlation.

cloud-infrastructure.title: Container Security — Image Scanning
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Scan images in CI and registry (ECR, Trivy) for CVEs before deploy; pin digests, not mutable tags.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Run as non-root, read-only root filesystem, drop capabilities. Use admission controllers in Kubernetes to block critical CVEs.

cloud-infrastructure.title: Kubernetes — RBAC Basics
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Roles bind verbs to resources; RoleBindings attach subjects. ClusterRoles span namespaces — avoid cluster-admin for apps.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Audit with `kubectl auth can-i`. Use namespaces for tenancy. Service accounts should have minimal permissions.

cloud-infrastructure.title: AWS GuardDuty — Threat Detection
cloud-infrastructure.summary: GuardDuty analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS for malicious activity — no agents required.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Enable in all regions. Suppress known benign findings after review. Export to Security Hub for centralized posture.

cloud-infrastructure.title: Cloud Shared Responsibility Model
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Provider secures the cloud (hypervisor, physical); customer secures in the cloud (IAM, data, OS patching on IaaS).
cloud-infrastructure.detail: SaaS shifts more to provider; IaaS leaves OS and app layers with you. Misconfigurations remain the top breach cause.

cloud-infrastructure.title: Cloud Misconfiguration — CIS Benchmarks
cloud-infrastructure.summary: CIS AWS/Azure/GCP benchmarks define hardened baselines — automate checks with Prowler, ScoutSuite, or Security Hub.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Prioritize public S3, open SGs, missing MFA, and unused credentials. Track remediation SLAs per severity.

cloud-infrastructure.title: Secrets Management — AWS Secrets Manager
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Never embed secrets in code or AMIs; use Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store with rotation and IAM-scoped access.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Audit GetSecretValue in CloudTrail. Prefer task roles over environment variables in ECS/Lambda where possible.

cloud-infrastructure.title: AWS Organizations — Service Control Policies
cloud-infrastructure.summary: SCPs set guardrails across accounts — deny root actions, restrict regions, or block public S3 policies org-wide.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Combine with centralized logging account. Landing zone patterns use OU structure for prod vs sandbox isolation.

cloud-infrastructure.title: AWS Lambda — Least-Privilege Execution Roles
cloud-infrastructure.summary: Each function needs its own IAM role with only required actions on specific resource ARNs — avoid wildcard policies.
cloud-infrastructure.detail: Watch for overly broad `s3:*` or `dynamodb:*`. VPC-attached Lambdas need extra ENI permissions. Scan env vars for leaked keys.

software-code-security.title: Fault Tree Analysis (FTA)
software-code-security.summary: Top-down Boolean model from hazard to basic events — cut sets reveal minimal failure combinations.
software-code-security.detail: Used in safety-critical systems (IEC 61508). AND/OR gates model component failures. Complements FMEA for systematic hazard analysis.

software-code-security.title: Secure Coding — Input Validation
software-code-security.summary: Validate type, length, range, and encoding at trust boundaries — never trust client-side checks alone.
software-code-security.detail: Allowlist over denylist. Canonicalize before validate. Separate data from commands (parameterized queries).

software-code-security.title: SAST vs DAST
software-code-security.summary: SAST scans source/bytecode statically; DAST probes running app. Use both in CI/CD pipeline.
software-code-security.detail: SAST finds early but false positives. DAST catches runtime/config issues. Track findings in defect lifecycle.

software-code-security.title: FMEA — Failure Mode and Effects Analysis
software-code-security.summary: Bottom-up analysis ranking failure modes by Severity × Occurrence × Detection to prioritize design mitigations.
software-code-security.detail: Used alongside fault trees in safety-critical systems. Document RPN scores and corrective actions to closure.

software-code-security.title: IEC 61508 — Safety Integrity Levels
software-code-security.summary: SIL 1–4 define required risk reduction for E/E/PE safety functions — higher SIL demands stricter V&V and architecture.
software-code-security.detail: Derive SIL from hazard analysis. Hardware fault tolerance and diagnostic coverage increase with SIL. Trace requirements to tests.

software-code-security.title: STPA — Systems-Theoretic Hazard Analysis
software-code-security.summary: STPA models unsafe control actions in complex systems — complements FMEA/FTA for software-intensive designs.
software-code-security.detail: Identify controllers, controlled processes, and feedback loops. Analyze scenarios where control is too early, late, or wrong.

software-code-security.title: Threat Modeling — STRIDE
software-code-security.summary: STRIDE categorizes threats: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Info disclosure, DoS, Elevation of privilege.
software-code-security.detail: Apply per data-flow diagram element. Pair with abuse cases and security requirements in design reviews.

software-code-security.title: Software Composition Analysis (SCA)
software-code-security.summary: SCA tools map third-party libraries to known CVEs — integrate in CI to block merges on critical vulns.
software-code-security.detail: Pin versions, monitor advisories, and plan upgrades. SBOM export supports customer and regulatory requests.

commands.explain: Check Node dependencies for high+ CVEs

software-code-security.title: Security Code Review Checklist
software-code-security.summary: Review trust boundaries, authz checks, crypto usage, logging of secrets, and error handling that fails secure.
software-code-security.detail: Focus diffs touching parsers, serializers, file paths, and SQL/command construction. Verify tests cover negative cases.

software-code-security.title: Memory Safety — Buffer Overruns in C/C++
software-code-security.summary: Unchecked bounds on stack/heap buffers enable corruption — use safe APIs, canaries, ASLR, and static analysis.
software-code-security.detail: Prefer `snprintf` over `sprintf`, bounded copies, and languages with memory safety for new components.

software-code-security.title: Integer Overflow & Wraparound
software-code-security.summary: Arithmetic on fixed-width integers can wrap, undersizing allocations or bypassing length checks.
software-code-security.detail: Use safe math libraries, validate before multiply/add for buffer sizing, and enable compiler sanitizers in CI.

software-code-security.title: Race Conditions & TOCTOU
software-code-security.summary: Time-of-check vs time-of-use gaps let attackers swap files or paths between validation and use.
software-code-security.detail: Use atomic operations, file descriptors instead of paths, and proper locking. Symlink attacks exploit TOCTOU on temp files.

software-code-security.title: Secure Coding — Fail-Secure Error Handling
software-code-security.summary: On failure, default to deny — close connections, reject requests, and avoid leaking stack traces or internal paths.
software-code-security.detail: Log errors server-side with correlation IDs. Generic user messages. Ensure finally blocks do not elevate privilege.

software-code-security.title: Software Supply Chain — SBOM
software-code-security.summary: Software Bill of Materials lists components and versions — required for incident response and regulatory disclosure.
software-code-security.detail: Generate in SPDX or CycloneDX from builds. Sign artifacts and verify provenance (SLSA levels).

software-code-security.title: Safety-Critical Verification & Validation
software-code-security.summary: V&V proves requirements are implemented correctly and the right requirements were chosen — independence increases with SIL.
software-code-security.detail: Unit, integration, system, and acceptance tests with traceability matrices. Regression on any safety-related change.

intrusion-detection-monitoring.title: Snort — Signature-Based IDS
intrusion-detection-monitoring.summary: Snort matches packet payload and headers against rules — fast for known attacks, blind to novel behavior.
intrusion-detection-monitoring.detail: Rule format: action protocol src/dst -> options (content, sid, rev). Tune thresholds to reduce noise.

intrusion-detection-monitoring.title: Sigma — Portable Detection Rules
intrusion-detection-monitoring.summary: Sigma YAML converts to Splunk, Elastic, Sentinel queries — share detections across SIEMs.
intrusion-detection-monitoring.detail: Map to ATT&CK tags. Version rules with status field. Test against representative log samples.

intrusion-detection-monitoring.title: SIEM — Correlation Use Cases
intrusion-detection-monitoring.summary: Correlate auth failures + success from new geo, impossible travel, and privilege escalation sequences.
intrusion-detection-monitoring.detail: Normalize timestamps to UTC. Define use cases before data ingest. Measure MTTD/MTTR per rule.

incident-response.title: Incident Response Lifecycle (NIST)
incident-response.summary: Prepare → Detect/Analyze → Contain → Eradicate → Recover → Lessons Learned. Document decisions in real time.
incident-response.detail: Containment may be network isolation, account disable, or WAF block. Preserve forensic images before eradication on critical incidents.

incident-response.title: IR — Containment Strategies
incident-response.summary: Short-term: isolate host/VLAN. Long-term: patch, credential rotation, monitoring enhanced detection.
incident-response.detail: Balance business continuity vs spread. Legal/comms approval before external notification.

incident-response.title: Post-Incident Reporting
incident-response.summary: Timeline, root cause, impact, actions taken, and preventive recommendations — audience-tailored exec vs technical.
incident-response.detail: Include IOCs shared with ISACs. Track control improvements to closure.

incident-response.title: IR Preparation — Runbooks & Contact Lists
incident-response.summary: Maintain current runbooks, escalation trees, and vendor contacts before an incident — speed under pressure depends on prep.
incident-response.detail: Include forensic tooling access, legal counsel, and comms templates. Test runbooks in tabletops quarterly.

incident-response.title: IR Detection & Alert Triage
incident-response.summary: Prioritize alerts by asset criticality, confidence, and blast radius — not every SIEM rule equals an incident.
incident-response.detail: Define severity matrix (P1–P4). Enrich with threat intel and asset context. Document false-positive feedback to detection engineering.

incident-response.title: IR Evidence Preservation — Chain of Custody
incident-response.summary: Image before reboot, hash artifacts, log who handled evidence, and store write-protected copies for legal admissibility.
incident-response.detail: Volatile data order: memory, network connections, then disk. Screenshot cloud consoles with timestamps.

incident-response.title: IR Eradication — Malware Removal & Patch Validation
incident-response.summary: Remove persistence, rotate compromised credentials, and validate patches before reconnection — partial eradication guarantees recurrence.
incident-response.detail: Hunt for secondary backdoors. Rebuild gold images when rootkits suspected. Verify IOCs absent in follow-up scans.

incident-response.title: IR Recovery — Service Restoration & Enhanced Monitoring
incident-response.summary: Restore from clean backups, validate integrity, and increase logging on affected segments during the watch period.
incident-response.detail: Define success criteria with business owners. Gradual return beats big-bang if dependencies are uncertain.

incident-response.title: Threat Hunting During Active IR
incident-response.summary: Hypothesis-driven searches across endpoints and logs to find related compromise beyond the initial alert.
incident-response.detail: Map to ATT&CK techniques observed. Use stacked aggregations in SIEM. Document negative findings too.

incident-response.title: IR Communication — Stakeholder Updates
incident-response.summary: Scheduled updates to execs, legal, and customers with facts vs assumptions clearly separated — avoid speculation.
incident-response.detail: Single incident commander approves external statements. Preserve attorney-client privilege where applicable.

incident-response.title: IR Legal & Regulatory Notification
incident-response.summary: Breach notification laws (GDPR 72h, state US laws) have clocks — involve legal early to assess reporting obligations.
incident-response.detail: Document decision rationale if not notifying. Contractual notification to partners may be shorter than statutes.

incident-response.title: IOC Sharing — ISACs & Threat Intel
incident-response.summary: Share indicators with sector ISACs and vendors under NDA — consume peer reports to accelerate detection.
incident-response.detail: Normalize STIX/TAXII feeds. Tune detections on shared IOCs with expiration to avoid stale alerts.

incident-response.title: IR Tabletop Exercises
incident-response.summary: Facilitated walkthroughs of ransomware, data breach, or insider scenarios expose gaps in roles and runbooks.
incident-response.detail: Inject complications (legal hold, media inquiry). Capture action items with owners and due dates.

incident-response.title: IR Root Cause Analysis — 5 Whys
incident-response.summary: Iterative why questioning finds systemic causes beyond the immediate vulnerability — fix processes, not just patches.
incident-response.detail: Fishbone diagrams help for multifactor failures. Track corrective actions in risk register to verified closure.

incident-response.title: IR Metrics — MTTD, MTTR, and Dwell Time
incident-response.summary: Mean time to detect/respond and attacker dwell time measure program maturity — trend quarterly, not vanity single incidents.
incident-response.detail: Segment by incident type. Pair with false-positive rate and tabletop participation for balanced scorecards.
